plausible_today: For U=Spec A minus V(J), the established theorem compares to the J-adic completion of the henselian pair(A,J). An m-adic comparison for arbitrary U with J≠m needs its own theorem.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Elkik’s exact complementary-open theorem is verified. The different completion ideals are the remaining issue; no exact general m-adic arbitrary-open resolution was verified by the searches.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly broadens the quantifier and gives no proof.
worth: High interest for one run to test the ideal-change step and find a sharp theorem or counterexample.

title: Fundamental groups of opens and formal fibres
as_he_states: Analogues are expected for π1, and geometric formal fibres are expected to have trivial topological invariants; π0 is said to be easy for good henselian rings.
plausible_today: Specify finite étale covers of the complementary open. Under excellence/normalization finiteness, compare their finite extensions using the henselian-pair theorem; distinguish this from triviality of π1 of every geometric formal fibre.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Elkik III Theorem5, p577, compares finite algebras étale off the completed ideal. Passing to all covers of an open requires the stated finite-extension hypothesis. The separate geometric-fibre π1 claim is not thereby proved.
why_open: The letter explicitly says it does not know the π1 assertion. Its π0 observation is recorded separately.
worth: Worth a careful category-level reformulation; a few hours can distinguish the two claims and verify the finite-cover case.

title: Higher Weil homology and homotopy comparison
as_he_states: The letter suggests analogous completion statements for all topological invariants definable for schemes, mentioning Weil homology and homotopy groups.
plausible_today: Choose a specific modern invariant, topology and coefficient system before stating a comparison. Finite étale π1, profinite étale homotopy and other theories are not interchangeable.
state_of_art: As of November2026: The opened Elkik theorem is a finite-algebra statement and does not settle an unspecified higher-homotopy assertion. No unique exact claim can be recovered from this broad programme.
why_open: The invariants are named but not defined, so later-theorem matching is underdetermined.
worth: Worth development only after selecting one invariant; no broad solved/open label is justified.

title: Analytic rings versus good henselian rings
as_he_states: The last paragraph asks whether complex analytic local algebras have significant intrinsic properties not shared by all good henselian rings in residue characteristic zero.
plausible_today: Separate Picard descent, completion surjectivity and analytic convergence. Complementary-open Picard comparison extends to henselian pairs, but the finite-length criterion for complete finite modules is specifically analytic and fails for already complete rings.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Elkik establishes broad henselian algebraization. The C[[t]] constant-elliptic example shows that the analytic necessity of finite length cannot be transported unchanged to every complete good henselian base.
why_open: This is an explicit conceptual question, not one theorem with fixed quantifiers.
worth: Worth a comparison table of exact properties; one run can already separate the analytic convergence effect from henselian algebraization.

title: Integral component stabilization
as_he_states: The abstract group lemma and tower proposition seek eventual constancy of components; connected-kernel injectivity is cancelled and geometric torsion-freeness is added.
plausible_today: Use commutative locally finite-type groups with finite-type transitions and the precise connected-kernel/torsion-free-cokernel conditions. Keep the full finitely generated integral component lattice.
state_of_art: As of November2026: The μ2→Gm example refutes the cancelled connected-kernel inference. Saturated lattices give the corrected stabilization mechanism. Kresch–Mathur §11.8 supplies the corresponding Picard Néron–Severi statement.
why_open: The cancellation and inserted hypotheses document the proof repair on the page itself.
worth: Worth a short complete lemma with hypotheses arranged in logical order.

title: Kernel versus cokernel and vector structures
as_he_states: The tower theorem has an ambiguous eventual kernel/cokernel clause and inserts characteristic-zero unipotence; the analytic letter states both eventual kernels and cokernels are vector groups.
plausible_today: For smooth commutative unipotent algebraic groups in characteristic zero use their vector-group structure. Without unipotence the projections E^m→E^n have abelian kernels and refute the vector-kernel conclusion.
state_of_art: As of November2026: The elliptic-product tower is computed. Kresch–Mathur §11 supplies characteristic-zero Picard deformation structure, but an exact opened reference for every analytic-group clause of i-bis was not identified.
why_open: The surviving word and inserted qualification materially change the theorem; the letter does not include a proof of i-bis.
worth: High value for an ink-led formulation audit before any abstract theorem is quoted.

title: Rational points of unipotent fibres
as_he_states: The group-scheme ML proof must pass to k-points, using vanishing of torsors under the relevant unipotent kernels.
plausible_today: In characteristic zero, use split smooth connected unipotent kernels, successively additive, so H1(k,U)=0. Retain the field and smoothness assumptions.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Kresch–Mathur §11.9 treats descent to rational points. The vanishing is the additive Hilbert90/vector-group step, not a consequence of group-scheme image stabilization alone.
why_open: The passage between functor points and actual rational points is compressed in the draft.
worth: Worth making this explicit in the final ML proof; otherwise the category has changed unnoticed.

title: Actual Picard groups and the Čech obstruction
as_he_states: After choosing a finite field extension, the draft writes Pic(Xn)→Pic-functor(k)→Čech H2 of a units group and marks the passage “rigoureux??” and “À expliciter”.
plausible_today: Use the precise descent obstruction for actual line bundles, state the units sheaf and its transition maps, and prove the required image stabilization before passing to kernels. Do not assume Pic(Xn)=Pic-functor(k) without a point/rigidification condition.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Kresch–Mathur Theorem11.11 proves actual-Pic ML for proper schemes over a complete noetherian local base containing a characteristic-zero field; §11.9 handles field descent. This is the exact modern benchmark for the omitted step.
why_open: The margin directly flags the rigor of this passage, and a stronger torsion-free-cokernel claim is cancelled nearby.
worth: High interest and tractable: rewrite the exact sequence with every map and obstruction specified.

title: Positive-characteristic failure of formal Picard ML
as_he_states: The letter says these results break down in characteristic greater than zero, without naming which clause or giving an example.
plausible_today: For a proper smooth scheme over a complete DVR of residue characteristic p, distinguish constant and jumping Néron–Severi rank; actual Picard ML is governed by that condition in the modern theorem.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Kresch–Mathur Theorem1.1/9.3 gives an iff with Néron–Severi rank constancy and supplies rank-jumping examples. Thus neither universal failure nor characteristic-free validity is correct.
why_open: The letter’s warning is explicit but unelaborated. The later example provides a mathematical explanation without assigning historical intent.
worth: Worth a worked example and a precise clause-by-clause comparison with the letter.

title: ML versus eventual constancy of the entire tower
as_he_states: The draft cancels stronger claims that the whole Picard tower is essentially constant or that excessive algebraization follows.
plausible_today: Retain stabilization of images into each fixed level. Allow nonzero and growing infinitesimal kernels, even in characteristic zero.
state_of_art: As of November2026: A constant elliptic family has nonzero additive transition kernels at all levels while all transition images stabilize. Kresch–Mathur proves ML, and formal existence addresses a separate compatible-system effectivity question.
why_open: The stronger formulations are visibly crossed out on scans258 and264.
worth: Resolved as a logical distinction; the elliptic example should accompany any statement of the theorem.

title: Formal projectivity from projective truncations
as_he_states: The proper formal characteristic-zero analogue should be projective exactly when all its thickenings are projective.
plausible_today: Prove actual-Pic ML for the relevant formal tower, choose a compatible class with ample closed-fibre restriction, then use the formal ampleness/algebraization criterion. If using an algebraic-model theorem, identify that additional assumption.
state_of_art: As of November2026: Kresch–Mathur Theorem11.11 supplies ML for proper algebraic schemes; Grothendieck exposé182 Theorem3 and Stacks088E give coherent formal existence for such a model. The abstract formal-scheme version needs the manuscript’s group argument or a separate formal theorem, not circular use of algebraization.
why_open: The letter announces the analogue and the draft sketches it; it does not isolate all category/effectivity steps.
worth: Worth a targeted proof audit because assuming an algebraic model would beg the intended algebraization question.
